Container.Name: oauth2-proxy
Container.Overview:
Puts a login in front of web apps that have none of their own. Your reverse proxy asks this container, on every request, whether the visitor is signed in; if not, the visitor is sent to your identity provider (ZITADEL, Keycloak, Authentik, Authelia, Google, GitHub...) and only comes back once authenticated.
Typical use: an Nginx Proxy Manager host with an "auth_request" block in its Advanced tab pointing here, so the app itself is never reachable without a login. One container can protect any number of sites: leave the redirect URL as a path only and it derives the right absolute URL from each request, and a shared cookie domain means one login covers all of them.
Every setting below maps to an oauth2-proxy option of the same name. The four you must fill in are the issuer URL, the client ID and secret from your provider, and the cookie secret. The ready-to-paste reverse proxy snippet and a step-by-step walkthrough are in the repository README.
IMPORTANT: this container is a gate, not a proxy. It is meant to be used with "Upstreams = static://202", letting your reverse proxy do the actual proxying. Anyone whose e-mail is in the allow-list file gets into everything behind the same instance, so use a separate instance for a different audience.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port your reverse proxy will point at. Nothing else should be able to reach it.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Folder holding the allow-list file. Mounted read-only on purpose.

Config.Name: Listen address
Config.Description: Address inside the container. Leave as is unless you change the port above too.

Config.Name: Provider
Config.Description: Keep 'oidc' for any standards-compliant provider (ZITADEL, Keycloak, Authentik, Authelia...). Other values such as google or github are also supported.

Config.Name: Issuer URL
Config.Description: Public HTTPS address of your identity provider, exactly as it appears in the 'issuer' field of its /.well-known/openid-configuration. No trailing slash.

Config.Name: Client ID
Config.Description: Client ID of the application you registered at the provider.

Config.Name: Client secret
Config.Description: Client secret of that same application.

Config.Name: Redirect URL
Config.Description: Leave it as a path only and the absolute URL is derived from the host of each request, so one container serves many sites. Every one of those sites must be registered as a redirect URI at your provider, as https://site/oauth2/callback.

Config.Name: Cookie secret
Config.Description: 32 random bytes, base64. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32 . Changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: Cookie domains
Config.Description: Domains the session cookie is issued for, comma separated. A leading dot covers subdomains (.example.com), so a single login is shared by every protected site under it.

Config.Name: Allowed redirect domains
Config.Description: Domains the proxy may send the visitor back to after login, comma separated. A leading dot allows subdomains. Anything not listed here is refused, which is what stops an open redirect.

Config.Name: Secure cookie
Config.Description: Only send the session cookie over HTTPS. Leave true unless you are testing over plain HTTP.

Config.Name: Session lifetime
Config.Description: How long a login lasts before the visitor has to authenticate again.

Config.Name: E-mail domains
Config.Description: Accepted e-mail domains. Set to * when you filter with the allow-list file below instead.

Config.Name: Allow-list file
Config.Description: File with one allowed e-mail address per line, inside the Data folder above. The container watches it, so adding someone does not need a restart. Without it, every account at your provider gets in.

Config.Name: Upstreams
Config.Description: Leave as static://202 when your reverse proxy does the proxying (auth_request). Point it at an app URL only if you want this container to proxy the traffic itself.

Config.Name: Behind reverse proxy
Config.Description: Trust X-Forwarded-* headers, but only from the addresses listed below.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy IPs
Config.Description: CIDR of your reverse proxy, for example 192.168.1.10/32. Fill this in: leaving it empty lets any client claim any IP address in the logs and in rate limiting.

Config.Name: Skip provider button
Config.Description: Go straight to the provider instead of showing an extra 'Sign in' page first.

Config.Name: Scope
Config.Description: OIDC scopes requested at login.

Config.Name: PKCE method
Config.Description: Proof Key for Code Exchange. Leave S256 if your provider supports it.

Config.Name: Pass auth headers
Config.Description: Return X-Auth-Request-User and X-Auth-Request-Email to the reverse proxy, so a protected app can know who is signed in.

Config.Name: Real client IP header
Config.Description: Header used to work out the visitor's address for logging.

Config.Name: Allowed groups
Config.Description: Optional: restrict logins to members of these groups, as they appear in the groups claim of your provider's token. Leave empty to rely on the allow-list file.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Container time zone, used in the log timestamps.
